params.body:
The concept graph left the projection on 9 November with the reading (#431), because most of what it named was written by a model: pattern names, tensions between concepts, and each signal titled by the classifier's note. Visitors liked the layers. This sends them again, made only of what can be checked.

## What changes

**`trendGraphForSite`** (`packages/core/trend-graph.mjs`) builds the layers under a trend:
- **signals:** the trend's own signals as the site lists them (`trendSignalsForSite`, so none from an inspiration-only source), titled by their own text. The old subgraph took any signal that mentioned a concept, inside the trend or not.
- **concepts:** the concepts those signals mention, at least two signals each, at most twelve, the most mentioned first. Archived concepts are left out, and so is a concept that names a listed competitor (Standard 0.17.0).
- **no patterns and no tensions.**
- No concept left means no graph (`null`).

**The projection** (`packages/server/heavy.mjs`, `projection-trends`) sends this graph in place of `null`.

## Deploy

Goes with the gentells-site PR that draws the layers again and keeps only these node types. Merged alone, the site keeps drawing no graph.

## Tests

- `npm test`: 1612 of 1612. `tsc`: clean.
- New: `test/trend-graph.test.mjs`. It covers:
  - the layers and their titles;
  - no single-mention, archived or competitor concept;
  - no signal from outside the trend;
  - the projection carries the graph without notes or pattern names.
params.title: Projection: the layers under a trend, measured only
